        significant instruction instability within 8 turns. Identifies attention decay as mechanism and proposes split-softmax,
        a training-free inference-time method that amplifies attention to system prompt tokens.
  residual_gating:
    description: Gating mechanisms for transformer residual connections and adaptive depth
    papers:
    - title: 'Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models'
      authors: Raposo et al.
      venue: arXiv 2024 (Google DeepMind)
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02258
      role: method-component
      relevance: top-k routing 动态分配计算。ThreadGate 可视为 MoD 在 turn boundary 上的特化
      abstract: Dynamically allocate FLOPs per layer via top-k routing. 1.5% loss improvement or 50% FLOP reduction.
    - title: Confident Adaptive Language Modeling (CALM)
      authors: Schuster et al.
      venue: NeurIPS 2022
      year: 2022
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07061
      role: method-component
      relevance: 置信度 early exit。CALM 是 monotonic exit，ThreadGate 允许 selective layer gating
      abstract: Dynamically allocating compute per input based on confidence. Up to 3x speedup.
    - title: 'Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free'
      authors: Qiu et al.
      venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Oral)
      year: 2025
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708
      role: method-component
      relevance: SDPA 输出加 sigmoid gate 消除 attention sink。可参考 head-specific sigmoid gate 设计
      abstract: Head-specific sigmoid gate after SDPA. Eliminates attention sink (83% to 4%).
    - title: 'SkipNet: Learning Dynamic Routing in Convolutional Networks'
      authors: Wang et al.
      venue: ECCV 2018
      year: 2018
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09485
      role: method-component
      relevance: 残差网络逐层 gating 先驱。ThreadGate per-layer gating 的前身
      abstract: Gating network to selectively skip convolutional blocks. RL+SL hybrid training.
    - title: Adaptive Layer-skipping in Pre-trained LLMs (FlexiDepth)
      authors: Luo et al.
      venue: arXiv 2025
      year: 2025
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23798
      role: direct-competitor
      relevance: plug-in router+adapter on frozen LLM 自适应 layer skipping。与 ThreadGate 高度类似，直接竞品
      abstract: Dynamically adjusts layers via plug-in router and adapter. Llama-3-8B skips 8/32 layers maintaining performance.
    - title: Learning to Skip the Middle Layers of Transformers
      authors: Lawson et al.
      venue: arXiv 2025
      year: 2025
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21103
      role: context
      relevance: middle-out layer skipping 负面结果参考
      abstract: Gating to skip middle blocks. Does not improve vs dense baselines at investigated scales.
  attention_manipulation:
    description: Methods that modify attention weights, positional encoding, or attention distributions to handle long-range
      dependencies
    papers:
    - title: 'Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation'
      authors: Press et al.
      venue: ICLR 2022
      year: 2022
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12409
      role: foundation
      relevance: ALiBi 在注意力分数上施加距离线性惩罚实现长度外推，是注意力操纵路线的代表方法，与 ThreadGate 残差门控路线形成设计空间对比
      abstract: Replaces positional embeddings with linear bias on attention logits penalizing distance. 1.3B model trained
        on 1024 generalizes to 2048 without fine-tuning.
    - title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation
      authors: Chen et al.
      venue: arXiv 2023
      year: 2023
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15595
      role: foundation
      relevance: 位置插值通过压缩 RoPE 索引扩展上下文至 32k，属于注意力机制内部解决长序列的路线，与 ThreadGate 在残差层解决多轮衰减形成对比
      abstract: Linearly down-scales RoPE position indices to extend context to 32768 tokens in 1000 fine-tuning steps.
    - title: 'YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models'
      authors: Peng et al.
      venue: ICLR 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00071
      role: foundation
      relevance: YaRN 综合 NTK-aware 和分段插值改进 RoPE 外推，代表注意力位置编码修改应对长程衰减的成熟路线，与 ThreadGate 机制不同
      abstract: Combines NTK-aware interpolation with ramp function for different RoPE frequency components. Extends LLaMA-2
        to 128k context with 10x fewer tokens.
    - title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
      authors: Xiao et al.
      venue: ICLR 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453
      role: context
      relevance: 发现 attention sink 现象（初始 token 聚集高权重），说明多轮对话中早期轮次 token 天然受偏置，ThreadGate 从残差路径角度控制历史轮信息保留
      abstract: LLMs assign disproportionate attention to first few tokens regardless of semantics. Retaining sink tokens
        enables stable streaming inference over 4M tokens.
    - title: 'LM-Infinite: Zero-Shot Extreme Length Generalization for Large Language Models'
      authors: Han et al.
      venue: ACL 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.16137
      role: context
      relevance: 用 Λ 形注意力掩码加距离截断实现超长上下文推理，揭示调整注意力掩码和调整残差门控是两条平行路线
      abstract: Applies Λ-shaped attention mask plus distance limit on position encodings. Generalizes to 200M tokens with
        2.7x speedup, no parameter updates.
    - title: 'Found in the Middle: Calibrating Positional Attention Bias Improves Long Context Utilization'
      authors: Ko et al.
      venue: arXiv 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.16008
      role: direct-competitor
      relevance: 直接校准注意力位置偏置修复中段信息丢失，最接近 ThreadGate 问题定义的注意力方案，审稿人会以此质疑为何不直接修正注意力
      abstract: Identifies U-shaped positional attention bias causing lost-in-the-middle. Training-free calibration redistributes
        attention to middle positions, improving QA by 6-15pp.
  theoretical_foundations:
    description: Theoretical analysis of transformer residual streams, information flow, and attention dynamics
    papers:
    - title: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
      authors: Elhage et al.
      venue: Transformer Circuits Thread 2021
      year: 2021
      url: https://transformer-circuits.pub/2021/framework/index.html
      role: foundation
      relevance: 提出残差流作为 transformer 各组件通信核心通道，直接为 ThreadGate 在残差连接处插入门控提供机制解释框架
      abstract: Linear algebraic decomposition of transformer computations. Attention heads and MLPs as read/write operations
        on shared residual stream. Formalizes induction heads and QK/OV circuits.
    - title: Toy Models of Superposition
      authors: Elhage et al.
      venue: arXiv 2022
      year: 2022
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.10652
      role: foundation
      relevance: 揭示残差流子空间叠加存储稀疏特征的机制，为 ThreadGate 按轮次条件化选择性激活残差通道提供理论依据
      abstract: Neural networks store more features than dimensions via superposition when features are sparse. Links polysemanticity
        to geometry of uniform polytopes.
    - title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens
      authors: Belrose et al.
      venue: arXiv 2023
      year: 2023
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08112
      role: foundation
      relevance: 逐层解码残差流隐状态揭示信息在深度方向渐进精化，支撑 ThreadGate 不同层门控强度差异化设计的动机
      abstract: Per-layer affine probes decode intermediate residual stream states into vocabulary distributions. Shows predictions
        iteratively refined across depth up to 20B parameters.
    - title: Exploring the Residual Stream of Transformers
      authors: Yu et al.
      venue: arXiv 2023
      year: 2023
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.12141
      role: foundation
      relevance: 分析残差连接对 logit 空间的加法效应，揭示知识参数跨层分布规律，为 ThreadGate 定位门控插入层提供实证参考
      abstract: Residual connections act as direct additive operations on pre-softmax logits. Identifies factual knowledge
        storage distribution across layers and modules.
    - title: 'Attention with Markov: A Framework for Principled Analysis of Transformers via Markov Chains'
      authors: Makkuva et al.
      venue: ICLR 2025
      year: 2025
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04161
      role: foundation
      relevance: 用 Markov 链理论刻画注意力深度依赖性，解释为何单层 transformer 无法形成归纳头，支持 ThreadGate 在多层残差路径施加门控的必要性
      abstract: Theoretical framework via Markov chain properties. Two-layer transformers learn induction heads on first-order
        Markov data; single-layer models get trapped in unigram minima.
    - title: 'From Self-Attention to Markov Models: Unveiling the Dynamics of Generative Transformers'
      authors: Ildiz et al.
      venue: ICML 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13512
      role: foundation
      relevance: 建立自注意力与上下文条件 Markov 链的精确映射，为分析多轮对话 token 分布随轮次漂移（GAR decay）提供随机过程理论基础
      abstract: Mathematical equivalence between self-attention and context-conditioned Markov chains. Output distribution
        sampled from context-weighted transition matrix.
  evaluation_benchmarks:
    description: Multi-turn dialogue and instruction-following evaluation benchmarks for LLMs
    papers:
    - title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
      authors: Zheng et al.
      venue: NeurIPS 2023
      year: 2023
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685
      role: foundation
      relevance: MT-Bench 多轮对话评测框架，是 ThreadGate 验证多轮 GAR 衰减修复效果的核心 benchmark
      abstract: Introduces MT-Bench (80 multi-turn questions) and Chatbot Arena. GPT-4 achieves >80% agreement with human
        preferences as judge.
    - title: 'Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference'
      authors: Chiang et al.
      venue: ICML 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04132
      role: foundation
      relevance: 基于 ELO 排名的人类偏好评估体系，衡量多轮对话模型综合能力的权威 leaderboard
      abstract: Chatbot Arena with 240K+ votes from 90K+ users across 50+ models. Bradley-Terry and ELO ranking validated
        against expert raters.
    - title: 'Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators'
      authors: Dubois et al.
      venue: COLM 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04475
      role: foundation
      relevance: 指令遵循自动评测标准，Length-Controlled 版本修正长度偏差，为 ThreadGate 单轮指令评测提供对比基线
      abstract: GLM-based length debiasing for AlpacaEval. Validated against 20K human annotations.
    - title: 'WildBench: Benchmarking LLMs with Challenging Tasks from Real Users in the Wild'
      authors: Lin et al.
      venue: arXiv 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04770
      role: foundation
      relevance: 真实用户多样化指令集，评估 wild 场景指令遵循能力，与 ThreadGate 关注的真实多轮对话性能高度相关
      abstract: 1,024 challenging tasks from 1M+ conversation logs. WB-Reward/WB-Score achieve 0.98 Pearson correlation with
        Chatbot Arena ELO on hard tasks.
    - title: 'MT-Bench-101: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Turn Dialogues'
      authors: Bai et al.
      venue: ACL 2024
      year: 2024
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14762
      role: direct-competitor
      relevance: 多轮对话细粒度评测体系，直接测量跨轮次能力退化，与 ThreadGate 研究的 GAR 衰减高度吻合
      abstract: Three-tier ability taxonomy, 4,208 turns across 1,388 dialogues in 13 tasks. Neither alignment nor chat-specific
        designs consistently improve multi-turn abilities.
    - title: 'MultiChallenge: A Realistic Multi-Turn Conversation Evaluation Benchmark Challenging to Frontier LLMs'
      authors: Sirdeshmukh et al.
      venue: arXiv 2025
      year: 2025
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17399
      role: direct-competitor
      relevance: 前沿 LLM 多轮对话准确率不足 50%，直接测量 ThreadGate 旨在修复的跨轮指令保留和上下文一致性失败
      abstract: 'Four challenge categories: instruction retention, user inference memory, versioned editing, self-coherence.
        All frontier LLMs below 50%; Claude 3.5 Sonnet tops at 41.4%.'
  exposure_bias:
    description: Exposure bias, teacher forcing, scheduled sampling, and train-test distribution mismatch in sequence generation
    papers:
    - title: Scheduled Sampling for Sequence Prediction with Recurrent Neural Networks
      authors: Bengio, Vinyals, Jaitly, Shazeer
      venue: NeurIPS 2015
      year: 2015
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03099
      role: foundation
      relevance: Scheduled sampling 首次提出用 curriculum learning 缓解 teacher forcing 与推理时 autoregressive decoding 的分布不匹配（exposure
        bias），直接支撑论文对 auxiliary attention loss 训练-推理 gap 的根因分析
      abstract: Proposes a curriculum learning strategy to gently change training from fully guided (true previous token)
        to less guided (model-generated token). The discrepancy between teacher-forced training and autoregressive inference
        causes error accumulation. Experiments on sequence prediction tasks show significant improvements. Used in the winning
        MSCOCO image captioning challenge 2015 entry.
    - title: Sequence Level Training with Recurrent Neural Networks
      authors: Ranzato, Chopra, Auli, Zaremba
      venue: ICLR 2016
      year: 2016
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06732
      role: foundation
      relevance: MIXER 算法直接优化测试时指标（BLEU/ROUGE）而非 token-level MLE，解决 teacher forcing 导致的 train-test discrepancy；论文中 auxiliary
        loss 同样面临 token-level 训练目标与 sequence-level 推理行为的错位
      abstract: Addresses the discrepancy between token-level MLE training and sequence-level generation at test time. Proposes
        sequence level training that directly optimizes test metrics (BLEU, ROUGE). Outperforms strong baselines for greedy
        generation on three tasks and is competitive with beam search while being several times faster.
    - title: 'Professor Forcing: A New Algorithm for Training Recurrent Networks'
      authors: Lamb, Goyal, Zhang, Zhang, Courville, Bengio
      venue: NeurIPS 2016
      year: 2016
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09038
      role: foundation
      relevance: 用对抗训练对齐 teacher forcing 训练与 free-running 采样的 hidden state 动态分布，直接证明 train-test dynamics mismatch 可导致长序列采样质量崩溃——与论文中
        gating 机制推理时失效的现象高度对应
      abstract: Introduces Professor Forcing, which uses adversarial domain adaptation to encourage the dynamics of the recurrent
        network to be the same when training and when sampling over multiple time steps. Acts as a regularizer improving test
        likelihood on Penn Treebank and sequential MNIST. Qualitatively improves samples especially for long generation horizons.
        Discusses trade-offs with Scheduled Sampling.
    - title: 'SEARNN: Training RNNs with Global-Local Losses'
      authors: Leblond, Alayrac, Osokin, Lacoste-Julien
      venue: ICLR 2018
      year: 2018
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04499
      role: context
      relevance: 基于 learning-to-search 理论统一分析 MLE 训练的两大缺陷：exposure bias 和结构化损失信息浪费。论文中 auxiliary attention loss 同时受这两个缺陷影响——token-level
        loss 无法反映 sequence-level attention pattern
      abstract: Proposes SEARNN inspired by learning-to-search (L2S) approach to structured prediction. MLE training fails
        to exploit structured losses and introduces train-test discrepancies (exposure bias). SEARNN leverages test-alike
        search space exploration for global-local losses closer to test error. Demonstrates improvements on OCR, spelling
        correction, and machine translation with a subsampling strategy for large vocabularies.
    - title: Quantifying Exposure Bias for Neural Language Generation
      authors: He, Zhang, Zhou, Glass
      venue: arXiv 2019
      year: 2019
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10617
      role: foundation
      relevance: 首次定量度量 exposure bias 影响并发现 LM 的 self-recovery 能力——即模型能从错误前缀部分恢复。这为论文分析 gating 机制在推理时的行为提供关键对照：如果 exposure
        bias 可自恢复，auxiliary loss 崩溃可能源于更根本的分布偏移
      abstract: 'Proposes sequence-level (EB-bleu) and word-level (EB-C) metrics to quantify exposure bias impact on quality,
        diversity, and consistency. Key finding: contrary to popular belief, distortion from prefix discrepancy is limited
        and does not appear incremental. Reveals an interesting self-recovery ability of language models that counters harmful
        effects of exposure bias.'
    - title: Sequence-to-Sequence Learning as Beam-Search Optimization
      authors: Wiseman, Rush
      venue: EMNLP 2016
      year: 2016
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.02960
      role: foundation
      relevance: 提出 beam-aware 训练将训练目标与测试时解码统一，量化 teacher forcing 的 train-test discrepancy 对序列生成质量的影响。paper_framing SP1 明确引用为
        exposure bias 在 sequence generation 中的量化先例
      abstract: Proposes a model and beam-search training scheme that extends seq2seq to learn global sequence scores, avoiding
        local training biases and unifying training loss with test-time usage. Outperforms attention-based seq2seq on word ordering,
        parsing, and machine translation.
    - title: 'Bridging the Gap between Training and Inference for Neural Machine Translation'
      authors: Zhang, Feng, Meng, You, Liu
      venue: ACL 2019
      year: 2019
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02448
      role: method-component
      relevance: 在训练时混合 ground truth 和 model-generated tokens 作为上下文，用 sentence-level optimum 选择预测序列。直接对应论文 W8 中讨论的
        exposure bias mitigation 实验方向——若应用于 auxiliary attention loss 可能缩小 30x gap
      abstract: Addresses exposure bias in NMT by sampling context words from both ground truth and model predictions during
        training, selecting predicted sequences with sentence-level optimum. Achieves significant improvements on Chinese-English
        and WMT14 English-German translation.
    - title: 'Why Exposure Bias Matters: An Imitation Learning Perspective of Error Accumulation in Language Generation'
      authors: Arora, El Asri, Bahuleyan, Cheung
      venue: ACL Findings 2022
      year: 2022
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01171
      role: theoretical-foundation
      relevance: 用 imitation learning 框架证明 exposure bias 导致 compounding error accumulation，且 perplexity 无法捕捉此累积效应。直接支撑论文核心论证：auxiliary
        attention loss 的 PPL 正常但 GAR 崩溃，因为 perplexity 掩盖了分布偏移对 attention pattern 的破坏
      abstract: Shows that exposure bias leads to accumulation of errors in autoregressive generation. Analyzes why perplexity
        fails to capture this accumulation. Empirically demonstrates that compounding errors from train-test mismatch degrade
        generation quality even when perplexity appears normal.
    - title: Scheduled Sampling for Transformers
      authors: Mihaylova, Martins
      venue: ACL SRW 2019
      year: 2019
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.07651
      role: method-component
      relevance: 将 Bengio 2015 的 scheduled sampling 扩展到 transformer 架构，通过 two-pass decoding 策略解决 transformer 非自回归 decoder 的适配问题。直接相关于论文
        Discussion 中讨论的 scheduled sampling 应用于 auxiliary attention loss 的未来方向
      abstract: Extends scheduled sampling to Transformer architecture via two-pass decoding strategy. Proposes structural changes
        to allow mixing of teacher-forced embeddings and model predictions during transformer training for exposure bias mitigation.
  gradient_conflict_mtl:
    description: Multi-task gradient conflict resolution, gradient surgery, and loss balancing methods
    papers:
    - title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
      authors: Yu, Kumar, Gupta, Levine, Hausman, Finn
      venue: NeurIPS 2020
      year: 2020
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782
      role: must-cite
      relevance: 提出 PCGrad，通过投影消除任务间梯度冲突。论文直接使用 PCGrad 做因果排除实验，证明梯度冲突不是 auxiliary attention loss 泛化失败的根因
      abstract: 'Proposes PCGrad: when gradients between tasks conflict, project one onto the normal plane of the other to
        remove the conflicting component. Demonstrates consistent improvements on multi-task supervised learning and multi-task
        reinforcement learning benchmarks.'
    - title: 'GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks'
      authors: Chen, Badrinarayanan, Lee, Rabinovich
      venue: ICML 2018
      year: 2018
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.02257
      role: must-cite
      relevance: 首个自动平衡多任务梯度幅度的方法，通过动态调整各任务梯度范数使训练速率一致。为论文中 auxiliary loss 权重调优的 baseline 和梯度冲突缓解方法的早期代表
      abstract: Automatically balances training in deep multitask models by dynamically tuning gradient magnitudes. Introduces
        a loss-rate-based gradient normalization algorithm that adjusts gradients to ensure tasks train at similar rates.
        Shows improvements on NYUv2 and other benchmarks.
    - title: Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent for Multi-task Learning
      authors: Liu, Liu, Jin, Stone, Liu
      venue: NeurIPS 2021
      year: 2021
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.14048
      role: context
      relevance: 提出 CAGrad，在共享参数空间上寻找与所有任务梯度最小冲突的更新方向。作为 PCGrad 之后梯度冲突解决方法的演进，支撑论文对该路线充分覆盖后仍无法解决 attention degradation 的论证
      abstract: Proposes Conflict-Averse Gradient descent (CAGrad) that minimizes the average loss while explicitly constraining
        the worst-case task performance. Finds an update direction within a ball around the average gradient that maximizes
        the minimum improvement across tasks. Achieves state-of-the-art on multi-task learning benchmarks.
    - title: Multi-Task Learning as a Bargaining Game
      authors: Navon, Shamsian, Achituve, Maron, Kawaguchi, Chechik, Fetaya
      venue: ICML 2022
      year: 2022
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.01017
      role: context
      relevance: 将多任务梯度聚合建模为 Nash 博弈问题（Nash-MTL），理论证明 Nash 均衡解优于启发式梯度操作。作为梯度冲突解决的最新理论上界，强化论文"即使最优梯度调和也无法修复 attention degradation"的论证
      abstract: Frames multi-task gradient aggregation as a bargaining game and proposes Nash-MTL that finds the Nash bargaining
        solution. Provides theoretical guarantees showing the Nash solution is Pareto optimal. Achieves state-of-the-art on
        multiple MTL benchmarks including NYUv2, QM9, and CELEBA.
  residual_scaling:
    description: Residual connection scaling, initialization, and zero-init methods for deep transformers
    papers:
    - title: 'ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth'
      authors: Bachlechner, Majumder, Mao, Cottrell, McAuley
      venue: UAI 2021
      year: 2021
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887
      role: must-cite
      relevance: ThreadGate 的 per-layer sigmoid gate 直接源自 ReZero 的零初始化残差缩放思想：x_{l+1} = x_l + alpha_l * f_l(x_l)，alpha 初始化为
        0。ThreadGate 将标量 alpha 替换为 turn-conditioned sigmoid gate
      abstract: Initializes each residual connection with a learnable zero-initialized parameter, enabling training of extremely
        deep transformers (up to 10,000 layers) without warmup or normalization. Achieves significantly faster convergence
        by allowing the network to start as identity and gradually incorporate layer contributions.
    - title: 'Fixup Initialization: Residual Learning Without Normalization'
      authors: Zhang, Dauphin, Ma
      venue: ICLR 2019
      year: 2019
      url: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09321

def add_to_literature_map(
    project: str | None = None,
    papers: Iterable[dict] | None = None,
    added_by: str = "",
) -> ToolResult:
    """Add (or merge) one or more papers into the literature map.

    Dedup: DOI exact (normalized) → normalized title → bibtex_key collision.
    Existing entries are merged field-by-field, never overwritten.

    Args:
        project: Project name — None writes to the global (idea-phase) map.
        papers: Iterable of paper dicts. Recognized fields:
                title, authors (list[str]), year, venue, url, doi,
                bibtex_key, category, role, relevance, abstract,
                semantic_scholar_id, source_idea_id, verified.
                Missing bibtex_key is auto-generated.
        added_by: Free-form tag for provenance ("paper-research",
                  "idea-generator", "user", etc.). Recorded on new entries.

    Returns:
        ToolResult.data = {
            "added": [keys],            # newly inserted
            "merged": [keys],           # matched existing, fields merged
            "rejected": [{title, reason}],
            "total_papers": N,
        }
    """
    if not papers:
        return ToolResult(
            success=False, error="No papers provided.",
        )

    paper_list = list(papers)
    added: list[str] = []
    merged: list[str] = []
    rejected: list[dict] = []
    now = _paths.now_iso()

    def _apply(data: dict) -> None:
        existing = data.setdefault("papers", {})
        for cand in paper_list:
            if not isinstance(cand, dict):
                rejected.append({"title": str(cand), "reason": "not a dict"})
                continue
            title = (cand.get("title") or "").strip()
            if not title:
                rejected.append({"title": "", "reason": "missing title"})
                continue
            if cand.get("role") and cand["role"] not in VALID_ROLES:
                rejected.append({
                    "title": title,
                    "reason": f"invalid role '{cand['role']}', valid: {sorted(VALID_ROLES)}",
                })
                continue

            existing_key = _find_existing_key(existing, cand)
            if existing_key:
                # Merge — fill empty fields, keep verified=True if either is True
                existing[existing_key] = _merge_paper(existing[existing_key], cand)
                merged.append(existing_key)
                continue

            # New entry — assign a bibtex_key if missing, dedupe within file
            key = cand.get("bibtex_key") or _generate_bibtex_key(cand)
            base_key = key
            suffix = 1
            while key in existing:
                suffix += 1
                key = f"{base_key}_{suffix}"

            entry = {
                "title": title,
                "authors": cand.get("authors") or [],
                "year": cand.get("year"),
                "venue": cand.get("venue") or "",
                "url": cand.get("url") or "",
                "doi": cand.get("doi") or "",

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Multi-turn dialogue is the dominant mode of interaction with large language models (LLMs), and system prompts that specify task goals form the foundation of instruction following. As conversations grow longer, however, models progressively lose track of these goal specifications. \citet{dongre2026attention} quantified this degradation across 12 models: the Goal Attention Ratio (GAR), which measures how much attention the model allocates to goal tokens in the system prompt, declines by 27--48\% between early and mid-conversation turns. We replicate and extend this finding on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, observing a 70.8\% relative decline in GAR from 0.0418 at turn~1 to 0.0122 at mid-conversation. We attribute the steeper decline partly to our use of last-token GAR, which captures summary-position attention more sensitively than the all-token average of \citet{dongre2026attention}, and partly to Qwen-2.5-7B's stronger instruction-following fidelity in early turns. This attention decay represents a systematic failure of multi-turn models to maintain task coherence, and it grows worse with each additional turn.
4	
5	A striking aspect of this degradation is what it does \emph{not} affect. \citet{dongre2026attention} showed that goal-relevant information persists in the residual stream throughout the conversation: linear discriminant analysis probes recover goal content with AUC\,=\,0.98 even at late turns where attention to goal tokens has collapsed. The information is present in the hidden states, but the attention mechanism fails to route it toward the output computation. This dissociation between information availability and information utilization suggests a natural intervention: if the residual stream already carries goal information, a learnable gate on the residual pathway could amplify or attenuate layer contributions to recover goal attention. This reasoning motivates ThreadGate, which modulates each residual update with a content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gate: $x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l \cdot f_l(x_l)$, where $g_l$ is produced by a two-layer network conditioned on the hidden state and turn features, inspired by the residual scaling idea of ReZero \citep{bachlechner2021rezero}.
6	
7	\begin{figure*}[t]
8	  \centering
9	  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig1_overview.pdf}
10	  \caption{Overview of ThreadGate and its failure mode. (Left) ThreadGate adds per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gates to the residual stream, trained jointly with an auxiliary GAR loss that targets goal attention. (Right) Under teacher-forced evaluation, GAR-ours reaches 0.50 across all fine-tuned variants; under autoregressive generation, it drops to 0.015--0.025, a 20--33$\times$ gap. The five-way comparison (ThreadGate, +PCGrad, Uniform Gate, LoRA-only, Base) shows that no intervention provides measurable benefit over LoRA-only fine-tuning.}
11	  \label{fig:overview}
12	\end{figure*}
13	
14	ThreadGate combines per-layer MLP gate networks with a joint training objective: next-token prediction (NTP), an auxiliary GAR loss ($\tau = 0.5$), and a gate diversity loss (\S\ref{sec:method}). The final formulation emerged from seven iterations spanning four loss families; only MSE target with gate diversity converged stably. To diagnose the failure, we construct a five-way controlled comparison (ThreadGate, +PCGrad, Uniform Gate, LoRA-only, Base) where each pair isolates one factor (\S\ref{sec:experiments}). PCGrad \citep{yu2020pcgrad} serves a dual role: training strategy and exclusion tool that rules out gradient direction conflict.
15	
16	Training succeeds: teacher-forced GAR-ours reaches 0.50 across all fine-tuned variants. The five-way comparison reveals that the failure is specific to autoregressive generation, where GAR-ours drops to 0.015--0.025, a gap exceeding an order of magnitude that persists across all training strategies. All four fine-tuned variants achieve indistinguishable performance (0.75\,pp spread on GAR-ours, identical PPL at 2.78); the gating contrast confirms that gates contribute zero measurable benefit. The PCGrad exclusion experiment eliminates gradient direction conflict without altering any outcome, establishing that conflict is neither necessary nor sufficient for the failure. These contrasts converge on exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled}, where attention patterns optimized under teacher-forced prefixes do not transfer to model-generated text (Figure~\ref{fig:overview}). An inference-time steering experiment provides constructive evidence that attention misallocation is a proximal cause: additive attention bias recovers autoregressive GAR from 0.064 to 0.727, bypassing the exposure bias barrier (\S\ref{subsec:steering}). A preliminary scheduled sampling experiment confirms that the gap is also mitigable at training time: GAR-ours increases from 0.016 to 0.318 (20$\times$), compressing the ${\sim}$31$\times$ gap to 1.57$\times$ with no PPL cost (single seed; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
17	
18	Our contributions: (1)~a systematic diagnostic framework for analyzing auxiliary objective failures in multi-turn dialogue, comprising a five-way controlled comparison that isolates four factors (turn conditioning, gating mechanism, gradient conflict, and fine-tuning), PCGrad-based exclusion via gradient surgery \citep{yu2020pcgrad}, and per-layer gradient conflict quantification (\S\ref{sec:method}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}, \S\ref{sec:analysis}); (2)~using this framework, the first empirical characterization of how exposure bias selectively destroys auxiliary attention loss generalization (20--33$\times$ gap) while leaving NTP robust, with evidence that token-level self-recovery \citep{he2019exposure} does not extend to auxiliary objectives, a preliminary demonstration that scheduled sampling compresses this gap from ${\sim}$31$\times$ to 1.57$\times$ (single seed), and cross-model confirmation on Llama-3.1-8B (27$\times$ gap); (3)~an inference-time steering experiment: additive attention bias at $\beta$\,=\,5 recovers autoregressive GAR from 0.064 to 0.727, providing constructive evidence that attention misallocation---not representation degradation---is a proximal cause under the tested conditions (Qwen-2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, UltraChat, GAR-family losses; \S\ref{subsec:steering}); (4)~a principled negative baseline: the final MSE formulation emerges from six failed loss families, and the five-way comparison rules out four alternative training strategies (\S\ref{sec:method}, \S\ref{sec:experiments}).

1	\section{Analysis}\label{sec:analysis}
2	
3	The five-way comparison in \S\ref{sec:experiments} established that gating produces no measurable benefit over LoRA-only fine-tuning. This section traces the failure through a three-step diagnostic chain: we first show that gates learn behavior opposite to the design intent (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}), then rule out gradient conflict as the explanation through an exclusion experiment (\S\ref{subsec:pcgrad}), and finally identify distribution shift as the root cause (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}). \S\ref{subsec:mechanism-specificity} confirms this selectivity with an orthogonal hidden-state metric, and \S\ref{subsec:cross-model} confirms the failure generalizes across architecturally distinct LLMs.
4	
5	\subsection{Gate Turn Conditioning}\label{subsec:gate-conditioning}
6	
7	The design intent of ThreadGate is to modulate the residual stream more aggressively at late conversation turns, where GAR naturally decays (\S\ref{sec:background}). We test whether the learned gates achieve this by comparing gate values at turn~1 (early) and turn~21 (late) across all 28 layers of the trained model.
8	
9	The gates do the opposite. In 27 of 28 layers, the gate value at turn~1 is lower than at turn~21 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test: $p = 3.73 \times 10^{-8}$, effect size $r = 0.975$). At layer~23, the gate is 0.769 at turn~1 and 0.979 at turn~21; at layer~14, it is 0.747 at turn~1 and 0.928 at turn~21. The pattern is consistent: gates suppress the residual stream more at early turns (where GAR is already high) and become nearly passive at late turns (where intervention is most needed). This inversion has a straightforward explanation. NTP loss pressure is highest at late turns, where the model must predict tokens conditioned on a long context. The NTP gradient pushes gates toward 1.0 to preserve the full sublayer computation, and this pressure is strongest precisely where GAR-based attenuation would be most useful.
10	
11	The resulting inference-time gate values range from 0.93 to 0.98 (2--7\% attenuation), far below what meaningful modulation would require; this explains the convergence with LoRA-only in Table~\ref{tab:four-way}. Figure~\ref{fig:gate-shift}(a) visualizes the per-layer gate difference. The inverted turn conditioning raises a natural question: does the NTP-GAR gradient conflict prevent gates from learning the intended behavior? If gradient conflict is the root cause, resolving it should rescue gate conditioning.
12	
13	\begin{figure}[t]
14	  \centering
15	  \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig3_gate_shift.pdf}
16	  \caption{(a)~Gate turn conditioning: per-layer gate values at turn~1 vs turn~21. In 27/28 layers, gates approach 1.0 at late turns, inverting the design intent ($p = 3.73 \times 10^{-8}$). (b)~Distribution shift: the 20--33$\times$ GAR gap persists across all five variants (TG, +PCGrad, UG, LoRA-only, Base), the gap persists across all five tested configurations.}
17	  \label{fig:gate-shift}
18	\end{figure}
19	
20	\subsection{PCGrad Gradient Conflict Exclusion}\label{subsec:pcgrad}
21	
22	The NTP and GAR gradients point in opposing directions across 68--79\% of layers throughout training, with mean cosine similarity ranging from $-$0.089 (epoch~0) to $-$0.042 (epoch~2). The NTP gradient magnitude dominates by 7.5--14.7$\times$. This raises a natural hypothesis: perhaps opposing gradient directions prevent the GAR objective from converging. If so, eliminating direction conflict should prevent the collapse. We test this using PCGrad \citep{yu2020pcgrad}, which projects the gradient of one task onto the normal plane of the other whenever two task gradients conflict. We apply PCGrad to gate parameters only, scoping our claim to direction conflict; magnitude imbalance \citep{chen2018gradnorm} and Nash equilibrium violations \citep{navon2022nash} remain untested.
23	
24	Eliminating direction conflict via PCGrad shifts per-step cosine similarity from consistently negative ($-$0.089) to oscillating around zero ($-$0.15 to $+$0.09), yet all outcomes remain unchanged: IID GAR-ours (0.50 vs 0.50), PPL (2.780 vs 2.784), and autoregressive GAR (0.015 vs 0.016) are indistinguishable (Table~\ref{tab:four-way}). $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ follows a nearly identical training trajectory and collapses in the same manner (Figure~\ref{fig:training-pcgrad}b). The exclusion follows by \emph{modus tollens}: if direction conflict causes the failure, removing it should prevent it; PCGrad removes it; the failure persists; therefore direction conflict is not the cause. Direction conflict is neither necessary (removing it does not rescue GAR) nor sufficient ($\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ converges during training despite persistent conflict). The 7.5--14.7$\times$ NTP magnitude dominance renders directional interference inconsequential. With gradient conflict ruled out, the question narrows: the training dynamics are not the problem (GAR converges under teacher forcing), so the failure must occur at the transition from training to inference.
25	
26	\begin{figure}[t]
27	  \centering
28	  \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig2_training_pcgrad.pdf}
29	  \caption{(a)~Gradient cosine similarity between NTP and GAR objectives. ThreadGate remains consistently negative; +PCGrad oscillates around zero. (b)~IID evaluation outcomes are indistinguishable: eliminating direction conflict changes nothing.}
30	  \label{fig:training-pcgrad}
31	\end{figure}
32	
33	\subsection{Distribution Shift Analysis}\label{subsec:dist-shift}
34	
35	Gates are ineffective because NTP pressure pushes them toward identity (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}), and this is not caused by gradient direction conflict (\S\ref{subsec:pcgrad}). The remaining question: why do GAR improvements under teacher forcing fail to transfer to autoregressive generation?
36	
37	The TF-AR GAR gap (Table~\ref{tab:four-way}) persists across all training strategies: the model learns the intended attention pattern on the training distribution but collapses under model-generated text. GAR-Dongre provides a revealing control: under standard teacher-forced training it remains uniformly low (0.01--0.02) with no distribution gap, so the shift selectively destroys the concentrated last-token attention pattern while leaving diffuse attention unaffected (scheduled sampling breaks this pattern; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
38	
39	The mechanism is exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled,arora2022exposure}: during training, the model conditions on ground-truth prefixes; at inference, on its own outputs. The statistical properties diverge, and the 2--7\% gate attenuation (\S\ref{subsec:gate-conditioning}) cannot compensate. \citet{he2019exposure} showed that language models exhibit token-level self-recovery from exposure bias, and our PPL results confirm this (Table~\ref{tab:four-way}). The critical distinction is between primary and auxiliary objectives: NTP is robust because it is the same task at both training and inference time, while GAR optimizes a distributional property of the input prefix that has no counterpart under autoregressive generation. Figure~\ref{fig:attention-heatmap} confirms teacher-forced GAR-ours remains near $\tau = 0.5$ (7--8\% decay, $N$\,=\,45), yet autoregressive GAR collapses for all variants (Figure~\ref{fig:gate-shift}b).
40	
41	\subsection{Mechanism Specificity}\label{subsec:mechanism-specificity}
42	
43	\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift} showed that exposure bias selectively destroys GAR-ours while, under standard training, GAR-Dongre remains unaffected. We test whether this selectivity extends beyond attention with an orthogonal hidden-state probe.
44	
45	We define Turn-level Residual Coherence (TRC) as the cosine similarity between hidden states at the last-token position of adjacent assistant turns. If exposure bias caused broad representational failure, TRC should show a comparable gap. It does not. For ThreadGate, teacher-forced TRC is 0.334 and autoregressive TRC is 0.332 (gap $= +0.002$). For LoRA-only, teacher-forced TRC is 0.349 and autoregressive TRC is 0.411 (gap $= -0.062$, reversed): autoregressive generation does not degrade hidden-state coherence. Neither checkpoint shows a TRC gap comparable to the 20--33$\times$ GAR collapse.
46	
47	The slightly elevated autoregressive TRC for LoRA-only likely reflects higher token-level predictability in model-generated text, which produces more self-similar hidden states. These results confirm the selectivity from \S\ref{subsec:dist-shift} with an orthogonal metric: exposure bias disrupts a specific learned routing behavior (summary-position attention to goal tokens) while leaving internal representations intact.
48	
49	Cross-model evaluation extends this selectivity: GAR-Dongre shows negligible distribution shift on both Llama-3.1-8B (AR/TF ratio 1.002$\times$) and Qwen-2.5-7B (1.28$\times$), compared to the order-of-magnitude collapse in GAR-ours, confirming that exposure bias primarily disrupts attention concentration at generation boundaries rather than aggregate attention patterns (the scheduled sampling experiment in \S\ref{sec:discussion} breaks this pattern, with GAR-Dongre rising to 0.353).
50	
51	\subsection{Cross-Model Generality}\label{subsec:cross-model}
52	
53	To test whether the failure generalizes, we replicate on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \citep{grattafiori2024llama3} with Base, ThreadGate, and LoRA-only. Phase~1 diagnostics confirm goal attention decay (GAR: 0.026$\to$0.003 over 10 turns). Teacher-forced GAR-ours ($N$\,=\,50) is 0.484 (TG) and 0.481 (LoRA-only); gating contributes zero benefit. We report median GAR-ours for autoregressive evaluation due to heavy-tailed distributions (5--8\% of turn-level measurements exhibit sporadic attention spikes). Median GAR-ours ($N$\,=\,20 mid-turn conversations, excluding the first two turns) is 0.018 for both TG and LoRA-only (Base: 0.009), yielding TF-AR gaps of 27$\times$ and 26$\times$. The TF-AR gap exceeds 25$\times$ on both architectures, consistent with the exposure bias hypothesis. The gate profile differs---Qwen's minimum at layers~3--4, Llama's at layer~25---yet both converge toward identity under NTP pressure.

1	\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	The failure traces to an incompatibility between teacher-forcing and GAR-family auxiliary losses, not to the gating architecture. NTP gradient pressure (7.5--14.7$\times$ the GAR magnitude) pushes gates toward identity (2--7\% attenuation), while inference-time steering ($\beta$\,=\,5) recovers GAR from 0.064 to 0.727, providing constructive evidence that attention misallocation is a proximal cause (\S\ref{subsec:steering}). Alternative hypotheses remain open: progressive attention drift unrelated to exposure bias, KV cache accumulation effects at long context lengths, or implicit label smoothing from the auxiliary loss could each contribute to the observed gap. Our evidence is consistent with exposure bias as the dominant factor, but does not exclude these alternatives. Split-softmax \citep{li2024measuring} offers a complementary inference-time approach that restructures attention computation rather than applying additive bias; unlike $\beta$-steering, it addresses the training-inference mismatch at the architectural level but cannot resolve exposure bias in auxiliary losses that require retraining.
4	
5	\paragraph{Scheduled sampling as training-time mitigation.} A preliminary experiment (single seed) applies scheduled sampling \citep{bengio2015scheduled}, linearly mixing teacher-forced and model-generated contexts. Autoregressive GAR-ours increases from 0.016 to 0.318 (20$\times$), compressing the ${\sim}$31$\times$ gap to 1.57$\times$ with negligible PPL change (1.38 vs.\ 1.36), consistent with exposure bias as a primary driver of the gap. GAR-Dongre also rises (0.019$\to$0.353), suggesting indirect improvement of all-token goal attention. The two paths are complementary: $\beta$\,=\,5 achieves the strongest GAR recovery but incurs 24\% PPL cost (1.43\,$\to$\,1.77); $\beta$\,=\,3 offers a more balanced tradeoff (PPL +9\%). Scheduled sampling incurs no fluency cost but requires retraining. A second seed trained from scratch (rather than resumed from a standard-trained epoch) yields AR GAR\,=\,0.418 (gap 1.20$\times$), versus 5\% seed variance in standard ThreadGate training, suggesting that early scheduled sampling exposure---before the model consolidates teacher-forced attention patterns---may further compress the gap; systematic schedule ablation is deferred.
6	
7	\paragraph{Instruction retention under steering.} Across 18 system-prompt constraint types, $\beta$\,=\,3 steering increases content constraint compliance by +23.8\,pp (GAR-compliance $r$\,=\,0.200, $p$\,=\,0.007; McNemar $p$\,=\,0.077), providing exploratory evidence for downstream benefit pending multi-model confirmation.
8	
9	TRC analysis (\S\ref{subsec:mechanism-specificity}) confirms the mismatch targets attention routing without disrupting hidden-state coherence. We scope claims to GAR losses on Qwen-2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B; magnitude imbalance \citep{chen2018gradnorm} and Nash equilibria \citep{navon2022nash} remain untested. Remaining directions include adaptive $\beta$ scheduling and layer-selective steering.

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

The failure traces to an incompatibility between teacher-forcing and GAR-family auxiliary losses, not to the gating architecture. Our evidence is consistent with exposure bias as the dominant factor, but does not exclude these alternatives. Split-softmax \citep{li2024measuring} offers a complementary inference-time approach that restructures attention computation rather than applying additive bias; unlike $\beta$-steering, it addresses the training-inference mismatch at the architectural level but cannot resolve exposure bias in auxiliary losses that require retraining.

The two paths are complementary: $\beta$\,=\,5 achieves the strongest GAR recovery but incurs 24\% PPL cost (1.43\,$\to$\,1.77); $\beta$\,=\,3 offers a more balanced tradeoff (PPL +9\%). Scheduled sampling incurs no fluency cost but requires retraining. 2

/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:5:\paragraph{Goal Attention Ratio.}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:6:We denote the task specification tokens in the system prompt as \emph{goal tokens} $\mathcal{G}$. \citet{dongre2026attention} defined the Goal Attention Ratio (GAR) for a model with $L$ layers and $H$ heads at turn $\tau$ as
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:7:\begin{equation}\label{eq:gar}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:8:  \text{GAR}(\tau) = \frac{1}{L \cdot H \cdot |\mathcal{R}_\tau|} \sum_{\ell=1}^{L} \sum_{h=1}^{H} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{R}_\tau} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{G}} A_{i,j}^{(\ell,h)},
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:9:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:10:where $\mathcal{R}_\tau$ is the set of response tokens at turn $\tau$ and $A_{i,j}^{(\ell,h)}$ is the attention weight from token $i$ to token $j$ at layer $\ell$, head $h$.
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:11:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:12:\paragraph{Two GAR variants.}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:13:\textbf{GAR-Dongre} is the original definition (Eq.~\ref{eq:gar}), averaging over all response tokens. \textbf{GAR-ours} restricts the measurement to the \emph{last token} of each assistant turn:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:14:\begin{equation}\label{eq:gar-ours}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:15:  \text{GAR\text{-}ours}(\tau) = \frac{1}{L \cdot H} \sum_{\ell=1}^{L} \sum_{h=1}^{H} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{G}} A_{t_\tau,\, j}^{(\ell,h)},
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:16:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:17:where $t_\tau$ is the last token index at turn $\tau$. Attention at this position reflects the information drawn upon for continuation; we use GAR-ours as the optimization target for $\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR}$ (\S\ref{sec:loss}).
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:18:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:19:\subsection{ThreadGate Architecture}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:20:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:21:Inspired by the residual scaling idea of ReZero \citep{bachlechner2021rezero}, ThreadGate modulates the residual stream with a content-and-turn-conditioned gate at each transformer layer. The gated residual update at layer $l$ is
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:22:\begin{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:23:  x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l \cdot f_l(x_l),
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:24:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:25:where $f_l$ denotes the sublayer computation (self-attention or FFN). The gate $g_l$ is produced by a two-layer MLP:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:26:\begin{equation}\label{eq:gate}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:27:  g_l = \sigma\!\bigl(W_2\,\text{ReLU}(W_1\,[\text{proj}(x_l);\;\text{emb}(t_d, t_i)] + b_1) + b_2\bigr),
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:28:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:29:[Omitted long matching line]

/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:31:\subsection{Training Objective}\label{sec:loss}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:32:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:33:The training objective combines three terms:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:34:\begin{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:35:  \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_\text{NTP} + \lambda_\text{GAR}\,\mathcal{L}_\text{GAR} + \lambda_\text{div}\,\mathcal{L}_\text{div}.
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:36:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:37:$\mathcal{L}_\text{NTP}$ is the standard next-token prediction loss. The GAR loss targets a fixed attention level to goal tokens:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:38:\begin{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:39:  \mathcal{L}_\text{GAR} = \text{MSE}(\text{GAR}, \tau),
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:40:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:41:where $\tau = 0.5$. GAR is measured at the last token of each assistant turn (GAR-ours, \S\ref{sec:background}). The gate diversity loss prevents collapse to a uniform value:
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:42:\begin{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:43:  \mathcal{L}_\text{div} = \text{ReLU}(\sigma_\text{min} - \text{std}(\mathbf{g})),
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:44:\end{equation}
/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_11/projects/turn_residual_gating/paper/sections/method.tex:45:where $\mathbf{g} = [g_1, \ldots, g_L]$ and $\sigma_\text{min}$ is a minimum standard deviation threshold. Both $\lambda_\text{GAR} = \lambda_\text{div} = 1.0$. We additionally tested three alternative loss families (cumulative, maximize, smooth saturation) across six configurations; only the MSE variant converged during training (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-loss}).
